{
  "title": "The Keeper’s Ember",
  "world": "Cinematic Storybook Realism",
  "cold_open": "The Atlantic does not whisper tonight; it roars, a grey wall of salt and iron battering the jagged coast.",
  "question": "But in the highest room of the hollowed tower, a steady, golden pulse begins to beat against the gale.",
  "journey": "Elias sits in the kitchen, his joints creaking like the floorboards. Outside, the wind howls through the cracks, carrying the scent of brine and old memories. He remembers his father’s hands—thick, calloused, and always smelling of kerosene. For three years, the great lens has sat dark, a glass eye blinded by dust and neglect. Yet, as the storm peaks, a warmth creeps through the stone walls. It isn't the house warming; it is the tower breathing. A rhythmic hum vibrates in the floorboards, a low frequency that feels like a heartbeat felt through the soles of heavy boots.",
  "discovery": "He climbs the spiral stairs, his breath misting in the freezing air. At the summit, the great lamp isn't just lit; it glows with a fierce, amber honey. There is no oil in the reservoir, no wick sparked by a match, only a light that seems to bloom from the glass itself.",
  "emotional_turn": "He reaches out, his trembling fingers hovering inches from the heat. He sees his father’s shadow stretched long against the masonry, not as a ghost, but as a lingering intention. The light isn't a haunting; it is a stubborn refusal to let the coast go dark.",
  "payoff": "Elias closes his eyes and rests his forehead against the vibrating frame. The roar of the storm fades into a hum. For one shimmering moment, the cold is gone, and the lighthouse stands as a bridge between what was and what remains.",
  "after_image": "A single, steady beam cuts through the spray, guiding ships that haven't sailed in years.",
  "hero_shot": "An old man’s weathered hand resting against a wall of glowing gold, while the storm rages in silence outside."
}
